bull_bear.body:
- Leadership position in the e-Municipality segment, supported by long-standing government relationships and domain expertise, used as a platform for adjacent solutions (Digital Project Management, Online Building Approval Systems, Accounting Reforms).
- Patented Sporecam technology (via associate Scanit Technologies) with potential dual-use across precision agriculture and a Human Allergy Network application.
- Pan-India sales team being leveraged to augment subsidiary InstaSafe's enterprise cybersecurity sales efforts.
- InstaSafe's Zero Trust platform positioned as purpose-built for the AI-driven enterprise threat landscape.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Moderation in profitability — Despite stable revenues, consolidated PAT declined to Rs 1,023.44 lakhs in FY 2025-26, impacted by investments and margin pressures as well as the long gestation period of Scanit's growth.
- Dependence on the government sector — The Company continues to derive a majority of its revenues from government contracts, which involve longer sales cycles and policy dependencies.
- Execution and cost pressures on large e-Governance projects — Large-scale projects entail execution complexity and cost management challenges; ABM has previously experienced time and cost overruns, impacting margins.
- Cybersecurity market competition — InstaSafe operates in a highly competitive global cybersecurity market characterised by rapid technological innovation.
- AgriTech commercialization risk — Scanit's business involves long gestation cycles, pilot validations, and gradual scaling, impacting near-term earnings visibility.
- AI technology disruption — Rapid advances in AI create a technology-disruption risk that requires ongoing investment in AI application within core business offerings to stay competitive; flagged explicitly as a risk area with an associated mitigation strategy.
- Customer concentration risk at Scanit — Scanit faced a revenue setback in 2025 due to the loss of a couple of major customers, highlighting dependence on a small number of large accounts; the Company has since pursued diversification to reduce single-account dependence.
- Scanit go-to-market and operational execution risk — Scanit continues to navigate macroeconomic pressures affecting farm-level technology adoption, longer sales cycles for large contracts, and the ongoing need to transition its SporeCam technology to full production-grade reliability.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: ABM Knowledgeware Limited operates across three strategic verticals - e-Governance, Cybersecurity, and Precision Agriculture (AgriTech). It provides e-Governance / e-Municipality software solutions (Digital Project Management systems, Online Building Approval Systems, Accounting Reforms) mainly to government, municipal and PSU clients in India; its subsidiary InstaSafe Technologies offers a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) and SaaS-based enterprise cybersecurity platform; and its US associate Scanit Technologies Inc. offers Sporecam(TM), a patented precision-agriculture and crop-disease prediction technology, with commercial pilots across USA, Europe, Latin America and India.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **e-Governance:** e-Municipality solutions, Digital Project Management systems, Online Building Approval Systems, Accounting Reforms, Digital Panchayat, BIM (Building Information Modelling) offerings
- **Cybersecurity:** Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) platform, SaaS-based enterprise security platform (InstaSafe)
- **AgriTech:** Sporecam (patented precision-agriculture / crop disease prediction technology, Scanit Technologies)
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- InstaSafe Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Classified as a Material Subsidiary of ABM as on 31 March 2026; provides cloud-based Security-as-a-Service / Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) enterprise cybersecurity solutions; ABM shareholding disclosed as 20.82% in Form AOC-1.
- InstaSafe Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of InstaSafe Technologies Private Limited (fellow subsidiary of ABM per related-party note), incorporated in the State of Delaware, USA, extending InstaSafe's global cybersecurity footprint.
- Scanit Technologies Inc. — associate: US-based Associate Company (35.20% holding per Form AOC-1) engaged in precision agriculture / AgriTech, owner of the patented Sporecam technology; ABM has significant influence via voting power; not consolidated on a line-by-line basis as it is not required to be audited under US law, so management-certified accounts are used for consolidation.
- Khaitan & Company LLP, Mumbai — related party: Enterprise over which Directors and their relatives exercise significant influence; counterparty for purchase of goods/services (legal services).
- Saffron Studios Private Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Directors and their relatives exercise significant influence.
- Lipsita Projects & Services Private Limited — related party: Enterprise over which Directors and their relatives exercise significant influence.
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- Leadership position in the e-Municipality segment, supported by long-standing government relationships and domain expertise, used as a platform for adjacent solutions (Digital Project Management, Online Building Approval Systems, Accounting Reforms).
- Patented Sporecam technology (via associate Scanit Technologies) with potential dual-use across precision agriculture and a Human Allergy Network application.
- Pan-India sales team being leveraged to augment subsidiary InstaSafe's enterprise cybersecurity sales efforts.
- InstaSafe's Zero Trust platform positioned as purpose-built for the AI-driven enterprise threat landscape.
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen core e-Governance business by leveraging deep execution experience while eliminating known time-and-cost-overrun risks through selective bidding.
- Expand presence in selective areas by continuing to build adjacent e-Governance businesses (Digital Panchayat, BIM, financial reforms, Online Building Plan approval) leveraging current domain strengths.
- Optimize cost structures and improve operating margins through selective bidding rather than volume growth.
- Scale the Cybersecurity business (InstaSafe) by leveraging ABM's pan-India sales presence to significantly augment InstaSafe's own sales team, strengthening Zero Trust platform capabilities.
- Continue investing in AgriTech (Scanit) via a dual India and Rest-of-World growth strategy, growing new solution categories (Digital Panchayat, Utilities, Infrastructure) and pursuing enterprise/global market expansion.
- Profitability and efficiency focus: work with alliance partners with complementing strengths; focus on talent development, domain specialization and execution excellence.
- Leadership and organizational strengthening via appointment of a Chief Revenue Officer to drive growth.
- InstaSafe: heading into FY 2026-27, focus on revenue consistency, enterprise account expansion, and deepening footprint in the BFSI and government sectors.
- InstaSafe: AI-era restructuring of teams and workflows to build a leaner, higher-output operating model.
- Scanit: strengthen positioning through SporeCam's differentiated field-level data capture, supported by an enhanced go-to-market initiative including a global lead-generation effort established in partnership with ABM.
- Explore dual use of Sporecam technology in a Human Allergy Network, pitching it to private and public health organisations.
- Capital management objectives are to safeguard the ability to continue as a going concern so as to keep providing returns to shareholders and benefits to other stakeholders, while maintaining an optimal capital structure to reduce the cost of capital; the stated strategy is to keep the gearing ratio within 1:1, with the Board able to adjust dividends paid, return capital to shareholders, issue new shares, or sell assets to reduce debt in order to maintain or adjust the capital structure. For FY 2025-26 the Board has recommended a final dividend of 25% (Rs 1.25 per equity share of Rs 5 face value), subject to shareholder approval at the 33rd AGM; the Company did not raise capital via new shares, bonus shares, differential voting rights shares, ESOPs, sweat equity, or buybacks during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No physical plant/capex expansion is disclosed; growth is footprint/geography-led across the three verticals. InstaSafe (cybersecurity subsidiary) has strengthened its global footprint through its wholly owned subsidiary InstaSafe Inc., incorporated in Delaware, USA, offering cloud-based Security-as-a-Service. Scanit Technologies Inc. (AgriTech associate) expanded its commercial pilots across the USA, Europe, Latin America and India during the year, and has grown its global footprint through a capital-efficient, distributor-led model with partners across the United States, Europe and India (via ABM); it secured its first multi-year commercial contract with a vineyard in Napa/Sonoma and achieved multiple renewals and customer expansions. Scanit also undertook a targeted diversification strategy to expand its customer base across geographies and segments after losing a couple of major customers in 2025.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian e-Governance sector continued to expand in FY 2025-26, driven by government initiatives such as the AI Mission, Digital India, Ease of Doing Business, and increasing adoption of digital public infrastructure (DPI).
- Demand for AI-enabled and AI-enhanced integrated platforms for municipal administration, citizen services, utilities management, and financial governance remains strong.
- Cybersecurity industry continues to grow rapidly, fuelled by increased cloud adoption, enterprise digitalization, and the shift toward hybrid work, with organizations transitioning to Zero Trust security frameworks.
- India's cybersecurity market is projected to nearly triple in size over the next decade, with over 16% of Indian enterprises planning significant cybersecurity budget increases.
- Agriculture sector is witnessing increasing adoption of AI-driven and sensor-based technologies to improve productivity and crop protection; several Indian states are launching Precision Agriculture initiatives with Central Government funding support.
- WHO has flagged a fungal disease risk affecting 300 million people worldwide, seen as an opportunity for dual use of Sporecam in a Human Allergy Network.
- Company continues to derive a majority of revenues from government contracts, which involve longer sales cycles and policy dependencies.
- Management expects short-term tapering in e-Governance revenues due to selective choice of opportunities, medium-to-long-term value creation from Cybersecurity and AgriTech investments, and gradual improvement in profitability as new segments mature.
- Scanit's market environment shifted toward a more pragmatic focus on automation and measurable ROI; SporeCam autonomously captures unique field-level data not available through conventional weather, satellite, or drone-based systems.
- Headline consolidated revenue reflected lumpiness in FY 2025-26 driven by the timing of a significant bulk deal in Q3 and billing delays on government projects in Q4; management characterizes these as timing artefacts, not demand signals, with the pipeline into FY 2026-27 reflecting underlying momentum.
- ABM has an order book of Rs 152 Crore to be executed in around the next 3 years, mainly driven by the e-Governance business as of now.
- Despite Q3/Q4 revenue timing lumpiness, underlying business momentum remained intact through FY 2025-26, and the pipeline heading into FY 2026-27 reflects this.
